title: The earthquake wave that crossed the Pacific 🌊
subject: tsunami
description:
Could a tsunami warning today stop this from happening again? 👇

On May 22, 1960, a magnitude 9.5 earthquake in southern Chile, the strongest ever recorded, sent a tsunami across the whole Pacific. It hit Hilo, Hawaii, about 15 hours later and Japan about 22 hours later, where nobody had felt the quake and no alert was issued.

Sources: Britannica ("Chile earthquake of 1960"), INGV Centro Allerta Tsunami ("22 May 1960: sixty years after the biggest earthquake ever recorded and the global tsunami"), USGS

scenes.text: A wave crossed the entire Pacific Ocean.
It began with a magnitude 9.5 earthquake in southern Chile on May 22, 1960.
The strongest ever recorded, it tore open a fault about 600 miles long.
Nearly 15 hours later, waves up to 35 feet hit Hilo, Hawaii, killing 61 people.
About 22 hours later it reached Japan, where nobody had felt the quake. No alert went out, and 138 people died.
Two days later, Chile's Cordón Caulle volcano erupted after nearly 40 quiet years.
